top.para: A reply to John Saroff's question about recommended readers and paywalls: no paywall, credit to start, a meter for what is read, nothing blocked, and a relationship kept on the reader's side.

in-short.para: The question; the answer in production; pay for what is read; nothing blocked; every link a gift; the reader's side; collages for new readers.

question.para: A paywall after a trusted recommendation, dark social rising from 7.1% to 11.3% of pageviews, gift links, and a share that can start a relationship.

arrive.line: No paywall, and credit to start
arrive.para: £5 of credit and no account; a few pence a page, charged for the share read; scrolling costs a tenth; a page not worth it is not charged; nothing blocked; top up after the value.

gift.line: Every link is a gift link
gift.para: Without a door to open, every share works in every chat and group, including the dark ones.

relationship.line: The relationship grows on the reader's side
relationship.para: A front page per persona in the reader's browser, reading sent by choice and encrypted, a newsletter, and an account that can live in the reader's vault.

take.line: What publishers could take from it
take.para: A free and complete first visit, charging after, letting readers decline a charge, keeping history with the reader, and treating every share as a gift.

limits.para: We are small; the dark social figures are Chartbeat's; the meter is client-side; my interest.

sources.para: John Saroff's post and card, the live pages captured for the collages, and my message of 31 October.
